title: Resistor color code practice worksheet with 10 blanks
summary: Ten four-band resistor exercises, with answers shown only after a choice.

blocks.heading: Read from the end opposite the tolerance band
blocks.body: These are four-band resistors: digit, digit, multiplier, tolerance. Write each resistance and tolerance on paper before choosing an answer. Each question reveals its worked answer when you select an option; selections last only while this page stays open.

blocks.heading: Band key
blocks.caption: Fourth band: gold ±5%, silver ±10%, brown ±1%. Color names are supplied so the exercise does not depend on color vision.

blocks.heading: Blank 1
blocks.prompt: Brown · black · red · gold → ______ Ω, ______ tolerance
blocks.explanation: 10 × 100 = 1,000 Ω. Gold in the fourth position means ±5%, or 950–1,050 Ω.

blocks.heading: Blank 2
blocks.prompt: Red · red · brown · gold → ______ Ω, ______ tolerance

blocks.heading: Blank 3
blocks.prompt: Yellow · violet · orange · gold → ______ Ω, ______ tolerance

blocks.heading: Blank 4
blocks.prompt: Orange · orange · black · silver → ______ Ω, ______ tolerance
blocks.explanation: 33 × 1 = 33 Ω; silver in the tolerance position means ±10%.

blocks.heading: Blank 5
blocks.prompt: Green · blue · red · gold → ______ Ω, ______ tolerance

blocks.heading: Blank 6
blocks.prompt: Blue · gray · gold · gold → ______ Ω, ______ tolerance
blocks.explanation: 68 × 0.1 = 6.8 Ω. The third gold is a multiplier; the fourth gold is tolerance.

blocks.heading: Blank 7
blocks.prompt: Brown · black · green · gold → ______ Ω, ______ tolerance

blocks.heading: Blank 8
blocks.prompt: White · brown · brown · brown → ______ Ω, ______ tolerance

blocks.heading: Blank 9
blocks.prompt: Red · violet · silver · gold → ______ Ω, ______ tolerance
blocks.explanation: 27 × 0.01 = 0.27 Ω; ±5%. Meter lead resistance matters when checking such a low value.

blocks.heading: Blank 10
blocks.prompt: Gray · red · yellow · silver → ______ Ω, ______ tolerance
